title: How To Thrive During The Upcoming Covid-19 School Year
author: Michael Linsin
summary: With policy details for the coming school year still unresolved, Linsin argues three fundamentals will carry teachers through regardless of what protocols emerge: boundaries, organization, and preparation. Boundaries, in the form of a proven classroom management plan, reduce reliance on verbal communication at a time when new protocols will make communication harder. Organization — a clutter-free, precisely run classroom — reduces distraction, which research links directly to better focus and behavior. Preparation covers both lesson planning and, more urgently, personal preparation: sleep, exercise, and leaving work at a reasonable hour so teachers have the mental reserves to absorb the year's inevitable surprises. He closes on a personal note, recalling his own first-year determination to make teaching work despite difficult circumstances, and commits to sharing strategies throughout the year ahead.
points: A clearly defined classroom management plan reduces reliance on verbal communication when new protocols make talking harder.
A clutter-free, well-organized classroom directly improves student focus and behavior, per the research Linsin cites.
Personal preparation — sleep, moderate exercise, leaving school at a decent hour — matters as much as lesson preparation this year.
Breathing, quietude, and visualization before students arrive help teachers stay calm and steady for the day ahead.
Teachers who lack strong organizational habits are likely to struggle significantly during a pandemic school year.
quotes: Sharply defined boundaries in the form of a proven classroom management plan protect learning, ensure fairness, and make managing behavior so much easier .
With a plan that every student understands inside and out, the teacher will have to do far less talking .

The happiest, most successful teachers are obsessed with organization and maintaining a pin-neat classroom. The reason, backed by science , is because fewer distractions equal better focus, listening, and behavior.

Being at your best and most rested will be more important than ever before. Sleep, moderate exercise , leaving school at a decent hour . . . these things will give you the physical strength and mental heartiness to handle the inevitable frustrations and surprises to come.
You must get to a place above the fray and craziness, so you can be the rock your students are going to need.
I was going to rack my brain and make a thousand adjustments if I had to to bring peace and joy to my classroom.
